symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries in each source vector, the length of the source vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the lengths of the source and target vectors, with $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta=t/s-1$ the relative gap between them.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries in each target vector, the length of the target vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the lengths of the source and target vectors, with $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta=t/s-1$ the relative gap between them.

symbols.name: relative gap
symbols.meaning: The relative gap $t/s-1$ between the target and source lengths.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the lengths of the source and target vectors, with $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta=t/s-1$ the relative gap between them.

symbols.name: source vector
symbols.meaning: A length-s vector, the input of the maps S, T and N.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a length-$s$ source vector and $b$ a length-$t$ target vector, so the letters $u$ and $b$ change meaning from the integers of earlier pages.

symbols.name: target vector
symbols.meaning: A length-t vector, the input of the maps C and P_t.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a length-$s$ source vector and $b$ a length-$t$ target vector, so the letters $u$ and $b$ change meaning from the integers of earlier pages.

symbols.name: source entry index
symbols.meaning: The index of an entry of a source vector, which is read modulo s.
symbols.quote: Entries of $u$ are indexed by $j$, entries of $b$ by $k$, and an index is read modulo the length, so $u_j=u_{j \bmod s}$ for every integer $j$.

symbols.name: target entry index
symbols.meaning: The index of an entry of a target vector.
symbols.quote: Entries of $u$ are indexed by $j$, entries of $b$ by $k$, and an index is read modulo the length, so $u_j=u_{j \bmod s}$ for every integer $j$.

symbols.name: source transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform on length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_s$ and $P_s$ be the normalized Fourier transform and the coordinate permutation $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ on length-$s$ vectors, and let $F_t$ and $P_t$ be the transform and the permutation $(P_tb)_k=b_{-sk}$ on length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ on length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_s$ and $P_s$ be the normalized Fourier transform and the coordinate permutation $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ on length-$s$ vectors, and let $F_t$ and $P_t$ be the transform and the permutation $(P_tb)_k=b_{-sk}$ on length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: target transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform on length-t vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_s$ and $P_s$ be the normalized Fourier transform and the coordinate permutation $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ on length-$s$ vectors, and let $F_t$ and $P_t$ be the transform and the permutation $(P_tb)_k=b_{-sk}$ on length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation $(P_tb)_k=b_{-sk}$ on length-t vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_s$ and $P_s$ be the normalized Fourier transform and the coordinate permutation $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ on length-$s$ vectors, and let $F_t$ and $P_t$ be the transform and the permutation $(P_tb)_k=b_{-sk}$ on length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: source-to-target weights
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian-weighted map from length-s to length-t vectors defined by $(Su)_k$.
symbols.quote: Let $S$ and $T$ be the maps from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors given by

symbols.name: target-spreading map
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian-weighted map from length-s to length-t vectors defined by $(Tu)_k$.
symbols.quote: Let $S$ and $T$ be the maps from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors given by

symbols.name: weight width parameter
symbols.meaning: The integer parameter that sets the width of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: The integer $\alpha$ sets the width of the Gaussian weights, which are bell-shaped functions of $j$ that decay quickly away from their centres.

symbols.name: selected coordinate
symbols.meaning: The integer nearest tj/s, ties rounded up, for an index j in the range 0 to s-1.
symbols.quote: For $0\le j<s$, let $\ell_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, ties rounded up, and $\beta_j=tj/s-\ell_j$.

symbols.name: rounding offset
symbols.meaning: The offset tj/s minus its nearest integer, for an index j in the range 0 to s-1.
symbols.quote: For $0\le j<s$, let $\ell_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, ties rounded up, and $\beta_j=tj/s-\ell_j$.

symbols.name: coordinate selection
symbols.meaning: The map that selects the coordinates $\ell_j$ of a length-t vector.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates, $(Cb)_j=b_{\ell_j}$, let $D$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, a map from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: diagonal factor
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map with entries $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$ on length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates, $(Cb)_j=b_{\ell_j}$, let $D$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, a map from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: near-identity operator
symbols.meaning: The map $N=CTD$ on length-s vectors, whose error from the identity is small.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates, $(Cb)_j=b_{\ell_j}$, let $D$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, a map from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: summation index
symbols.meaning: The summation index running over all integers in the expansion of $(Nu)_j$.
symbols.quote: The same rule defines $\ell_i$ and $\beta_i$ for every integer $i$, the summation index over all integers used below.

symbols.name: error operator
symbols.meaning: The error $E=I-N$ of the near-identity operator N.
symbols.quote: Write $N=I-E$, where $E=I-N$ is the error, so $\|E\|=\|N-I\|$.

symbols.name: identity map
symbols.meaning: The identity map on length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: Here $I$ is the identity map on length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: precision parameter
symbols.meaning: The integer precision parameter of the cited estimate, with p greater than 100.
symbols.quote: Here $p>100$ is an integer precision parameter, and the estimate applies when $\alpha$ is an integer with $2\le\alpha<p$, $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta>p/\alpha^4$.

symbols.name: Neumann index
symbols.meaning: The summation index of the Neumann series of powers of E.
symbols.quote: The Neumann series $\sum_{r\ge0}E^r$, with $r$ its summation index, is the operator version of the geometric series.

symbols.name: last partial-sum index
symbols.meaning: The last index of a partial sum of the Neumann series.
symbols.quote: Let $M$ be the last index of a partial sum $\sum_{r=0}^{M}E^r$.

symbols.name: source contraction map
symbols.meaning: The map A=S from length-s to length-t vectors in the factored identity.
symbols.quote: This has the form $P_sF_s=BP_tF_tA$, where $A=S$ and $B=DN^{-1}C$ are linear maps.

symbols.name: target contraction map
symbols.meaning: The map $B=DN^{-1}C$ from length-t to length-s vectors in the factored identity.
symbols.quote: This has the form $P_sF_s=BP_tF_tA$, where $A=S$ and $B=DN^{-1}C$ are linear maps.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling replaces a [discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, using Gaussian weights to move between the two sets of frequencies.
It replaces the transforms for the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of two integers by such transforms.
The other terms form $N-I$, whose size is measured in the [operator norm](operator-norm.md) for the maximum-modulus vector norm.
